To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) T cell proliferative responses to influenza A and alloantigen are decreased in HIV-infected patients compared with healthy controls, (2) HIV-specific proliferative responses are not associated with increased IL-10 production, (3) influenza-specific CTL responses correlate with CD4+ T cell counts and T cell proliferation in HIV-infected individuals, (4) HAART-treated asymptotic patients have T cell responses that are comparable to those of healthy controls, and (5) HAART-treated

HIV-infected patients have decreased T cell responses to influenza A virus and alloantigen, but not HIV-1 antigents, and that HAART-treated patients, but not patients who did not receive HAART, have T cell proliferative responses comparable to those observed in control individuals.
HAART-treated HIV-infected patients, but not untreated patients with advanced HIV disease, have T cell immune responses that are comparable to those of healthy control subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of HAART on T cell immunity in HIV-infected patients and the role of T cells in the control of HIV infection.
the effects of highly active antiviral therapy (HAAT) on immune responses in patients with HIV infection.
the effects of HIV-1 on the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAART-treated patients have T cell responses similar to those of control subjects, whereas AIDS patients do not.
HIV infection, even with long-term antiretrovirus therapy, results in an impaired immune response to recall antigens and alloantigens and that this impairment is not fully reversible by the therapy.
the T cell immune responses in HIV-infected patients are not restored to the level of uninfected individuals by the administration of HAART.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HAART is a very effective treatment in controlling HIV-1 replication, but the effect on immune reconstitution is limited.
HAART-treated patients, but not patients who are still in advanced disease, are able to mount normal immune responses.
HAART is effective in reversing the immunodeficiency in HIV-infected patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is not completely destroyed by HIV and that it is possible to reinvigorate the immune system with immune based therapy.
the T cell responses of HIV patients are not restored after HAART treatment.
HAART is effective in restoring the immune system in asymptomatic patients, and it is important to continue the therapy to prevent disease progression.
